newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourses set aside row on cooperation plan.
newsitem.headline: German bourses set aside row on cooperation plan.

text.p: Germany's regional bourses have ended a long-running dispute over nationwide cooperation and all eight will take part in a new national link-up from July 1, German bourse group Deutsche Boerse AG said on Tuesday.

The new national link-up is aimed at harmonising prices at the eight German bourses. Smaller stock exchanges in Stuttgart, Hanover, Hamburg and Bremen will join their larger counterparts in Frankfurt, Munich, Berlin and Duesseldorf in the pact.

Werner Seifert, management board chairman of Deutsche Boerse AG, said at the group's annual news conference that the new cooperation pact "embodies the principle of one price per security at the same time".
Seifert said the link-up it would remove the "embarrassing price differences" between the regional bourses which have led to "arbitrage" on shares quoted on more than one exchange.
Arbitrage is where dealers exploit market imperfections, such as the existence of more than one price for a security, to trade securities at a profit.

Earlier attempts by the exchanges to cooperate have foundered on the fears of the smaller stock exchanges that they would as a result lose business and influence to the powerful shadow of the Frankfurt bourse.
Stuttgart, Hanover, Hamburg and Bremen appealed to the cartel authorities late last year to ensure their competitive positions were not in danger.
There was as yet no decision on how the individual shares would be divided among the different stock exchanges.
Seifert said that the decision to come up with the pact and iron out the price differences was made with the investor in mind, rather than catering to stock exchange politics.
